title: Mizzen access policy
description: A versioned access policy: independent capabilities, a semantic read allowlist, write paths and scope, named check runners, network destinations and stages, and per-capability approvals. `parseAccessPolicy` in `src/permissions/policy.ts` validates against this schema, fills least-privilege defaults, and reports every problem with its JSON Pointer. An absent policy grants public read only.

task.description: The task this policy belongs to; defaults to `site`.

capabilities.description: The independent switches. Omitted capabilities are false except read.

read.description: Read public or allowed content. Default true.

write.description: Write through the write policy. Default false.

execute.description: Run a named check runner. Default false.

network.description: Reach an allowed destination in an allowed stage. Default false.

read.description: Public content, allowed audiences, and optional page, block, collection, and field allowlists.

public.description: Whether content without an audience is readable. Default true.

audiences.description: Audiences the task may read. Empty means public only.

pages.description: Page URLs, source paths, ids, or globs. Absent means every public page.

blocks.description: Block ids or globs. Absent means every block of a readable page.

collections.description: Collection names. Absent means no collection data.

fields.description: Per-collection field allowlist. A collection left out publishes no field.

write.description: An allowed path list and a semantic scope; both must allow a write.

paths.description: Site-relative paths or globs the task may write.

scope.description: The pages, blocks, collections, or files the write is about. At least one entry is required.

check.description: Named check runners. A runner grant never allows an arbitrary command or the network.

runners.description: Runners the task may execute, each with its own input and resource allowlist.

network.description: Explicit destinations and the stages they are allowed in. Both must match.

approvals.description: Capabilities that need a separate, explicit approval. Default: write, execute, network, and publish.

path.description: A site-relative path or glob with forward slashes: no leading slash, drive letter, backslash, or `..` segment.

destination.description: An absolute URL, a host name, or `*`; a scheme-less value is a host.
